children: The Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi) has upgraded its holiday home regulatory system, aiming to streamline licensing, improve compliance and provide owners, operators and sector partners with a more efficient digital experience.
The enhanced platform reduces approval times, simplifies licensing procedures and strengthens integration with government entities.

It also introduces improved tools for revenue management, monitoring, inspections and compliance tracking, helping holiday home operators maintain quality and safety standards while meeting regulatory requirements.

Hamad Alsudain, Acting Executive Director of Support Services at DCT Abu Dhabi, said: “The holiday homes sector continues to experience robust growth, driven by greater transparency and enhanced efficiency and an increasingly user-friendly operating environment. These advances further strengthen Abu Dhabi’s position as a world-class tourism destination. The current improvements reflect our ongoing commitment to digital transformation and honour DCT Abu Dhabi’s commitment under Tourism Strategy 2030 to further enhance the holiday home segment to diversify accommodation options.”
The updated system has also been designed to comply with data protection requirements, with safeguards for the secure management and storage of sensitive information.

The latest upgrades build on changes introduced in 2024, when DCT Abu Dhabi worked with government stakeholders to integrate its licensing platform with the Department of Municipalities and Transport and the self-inspection system.
That integration helped reduce holiday home permit issuance times to less than six hours.
The latest developments further support Abu Dhabi’s efforts to expand accommodation choices and enhance the regulatory environment as the emirate continues to grow its tourism sector.

title: ZAWYA: DCT Abu Dhabi enhances holiday home regulations with new digital system
